title: A run whose finish row fails to write vanishes from the run list
body:
## Summary
finish_run removes the run from `runs` before appending its run.finish audit row and only pushes it to `run_history` after that write succeeds; a failed write drops the run from both.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:398-415 (finish_run): `self.runs.remove(&run)`, then `app(append_audit(..))?`, then `run_history.push`. On Err the snapshot is in neither list, so run_snapshots() no longer contains it and the actor's diff (crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:618-627) never emits its end state; the Runs read and the UI keep the last state they saw (Running). The Fault event names no run. Fixed: push the ended snapshot to run_history before the audit write, and still return the error.

## Flow
- engine finishes -> Message::EngineFinished -> finish_run
- audit append fails (disk full, ledger fault) -> `?` returns before run_history.push
- Runs read: run absent; the UI still shows it Running

## Expected impact
The owner no longer sees a finished run as still running until a restart. Nothing should break: the audit gap is still reported as a Fault.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - an ended run is always shown as ended
Before: walked: on Err the run is removed from both collections
After: the run is listed with its end state even when the audit write fails
Method: simulation - no test seam makes Ledger::append_audit fail from table-runtime; needs a #[cfg(test)] fault flag like fail_rungs (service.rs:174)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs finish_run: let Some(mut active) = self.runs.remove(&run) ... app(self.pipeline.wallet.ledger.append_audit(..))?; ... self.run_history.push(snapshot.clone());
instrument: add #[cfg(test)] fail_run_audit to Runtime (like fail_rungs) and finish a run with it set: assert run_snapshots() holds the run with its end state and the call returns Err; red today

title: Refusal-trail gap counters are kept but never shown
body:
## Summary
RefusalLog.unrecorded and .write_failures count refused privileged commands that the audit chain did not record. Nothing outside one test reads them.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/dispatcher.rs:21-29 documents them as 'the trail's known gaps'. grep 'unrecorded|write_failures' over crates finds only dispatcher.rs and crates/table-runtime/src/refusal_audit_tests.rs:97. No owner_facts, safety_record, proof or event field carries them, so a probe loop over the 60-per-minute cap, or a failing audit write, leaves no visible trace. Fixed: surface both counts in the safety record (or owner_facts) as refusals not recorded since start.

## Flow
- a window probes a privileged command more than 60 times in a minute
- rows 61+ only increment refusals.unrecorded
- no surface reads the counter

## Expected impact
The owner, and anyone reading a proof, learns that the refusal trail has gaps. Possible breakage: a closed type gains a field, so the bindings need regenerating.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - known audit gaps are visible
Before: readers of the 2 counters outside tests: 0
After: 1 surface shows both
Method: simulation - the surface lives in safety.rs / table-client types (other contexts)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: after 61 refused privileged calls in one window, safety_record (or owner_facts) reports unrecorded=1; red today

title: Tumbler card actions rebuild the whole attention snapshot for one deal
body:
## Summary
ClaimNotification, LetLapse, Snooze and the ladder's card()/due_gate() call attention(), which folds every deal, the exposure view and the forecast, and writes rungs, only to check one deal's card.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/dispatcher.rs:315, :655 and :672 and crates/table-runtime/src/ladder.rs:76-91 each call self.attention() (dispatcher.rs:192-280: list_deals, per-deal money_check/preferences/display_number/deadline, envelope_view, forecast, record_snapshot_rungs). One Tumbler click costs as much as the 1 s publish pass. Fixed: build the one deal's AttentionSource/item (the loop body of attention() for that deal) and keep the snooze/lapse rules identical.

## Flow
- owner clicks Snooze on a card
- attention() walks all N deals plus the forecast
- one item is kept

## Expected impact
Card actions stay O(1) in the number of deals as the book grows. Possible breakage: the single-deal item must match the snapshot's item exactly; a parity test pins it.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - a card action reads one deal
Before: ledger reads per ClaimNotification grow with N deals (whole fold + forecast)
After: constant in N
Method: simulation - needs a counting ledger/forecast seam
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/dispatcher.rs:315 self.attention()?.items.iter().any(..); :655 and :672 the same; crates/table-runtime/src/ladder.rs:77 self.attention().ok()?
instrument: count forecast()/list_deals calls per ClaimNotification at N=1 and N=20 deals (cfg(test) counter) and assert they are equal; plus a parity test that the single-deal item equals the snapshot item

title: One engine's workspace failure stops the other engine being attached
body:
## Summary
attach_native_engines returns on the first NativeEngine::new error. A claude-code workspace failure therefore leaves codex-cli unattached, and both read 'Executable not resolved'.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs attach_native_engines: `NativeEngine::new(..).map_err(..)?` inside the per-engine loop. The loop's later engine is never probed, and engine_info() reports it with the wrong reason. Fixed: record an unavailable EngineInfo with reason 'Engine workspace unavailable' and continue.

## Flow
- two CLIs resolve on PATH
- the first engine's workspace dir cannot be created
- attach returns Err; the second engine is never attached

## Expected impact
The owner can still pick the engine that works, and sees the true reason for the one that does not. Nothing should break: attach already tolerates a failed probe.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - each engine attaches independently
Before: walked: 1 failure -> 2 engines unavailable
After: 1 failure -> 1 unavailable
Method: simulation - resolve_command reads the real PATH; needs an injectable resolver
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs: for id in [EngineId::ClaudeCode, EngineId::CodexCli] { ... .map_err(|_| unavailable("Engine workspace unavailable"))?; }
instrument: split the loop body into fn attach_one(id, executable, root) and test it with a root that is a file: the other engine is still attached, and the reason names the workspace

title: table-runtime declares four dependencies outside the workspace table
body:
## Summary
table-runtime pins zeroize = "1" and takes table-relay, table-mcp and table-verify by path, while every other internal crate uses `.workspace = true`.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/Cargo.toml: `table-relay = { path = "../table-relay" }`, `table-mcp = {path="../table-mcp"}`, `zeroize = "1"`, `table-verify = {path="../table-verify"}`; the root Cargo.toml has no zeroize entry. Two version sources for one dependency is how a workspace drifts. Fixed: add them to [workspace.dependencies] and inherit.

## Flow
- grep zeroize Cargo.toml -> absent from workspace
- crates/table-runtime/Cargo.toml declares it locally

## Expected impact
Every internal and shared version is stated in one place. Nothing should break if the versions match (diff cargo tree before and after).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - single version source
Before: 4 non-workspace declarations
After: 0
Method: probe - read the manifests; no build was run because the file is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: cargo tree -p table-runtime identical before/after; non-workspace declarations 4 -> 0

title: Release builds discard every runtime diagnostic
body:
## Summary
The runtime writes its diagnostics with eprintln!, but the release desktop app runs under windows_subsystem="windows", where stderr goes nowhere. ladder.rs's doc comment says a failed rung is 'logged'.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/configuration.rs:519 and crates/table-runtime/src/ladder.rs:43 use eprintln!; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:1 sets windows_subsystem="windows" for release; crates/table-runtime/src/ladder.rs:5 claims 'logged and dropped'. The product has no log crate or sink, so choosing one (rolling file, audit row, event) is a product decision.

## Flow
- release build, a rung write fails
- eprintln! goes to a detached stderr
- no trace anywhere

## Expected impact
Support can see why a rung or a credential date was not recorded. Possible breakage: the sink must never carry secrets or counterparty text.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a diagnostic sink exists
Before: 2 production eprintln! sites with no sink in release
After: a chosen sink
Method: simulation - a decision, not a measurement
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:1 #![cfg_attr(all(windows, not(debug_assertions)), windows_subsystem = "windows")]; crates/table-runtime/src/ladder.rs:43 eprintln!("The Table: an attention rung could not be recorded");
